pr_body:
- Use a `ThrottledTaskRunner` on top of the `SNAPSHOT_META` threadpool for snapshot delete tasks.
- Use the `SNAPSHOT_META` threadpool for some of the snapshot metadata update and finzalization tasks.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93220
pr_title: Shift more work to the snapshot_meta pool
pr_comment: One question in this area for my learning: how come `SNAPSHOT_META` has such a large size?

The reason I am asking is to understand whether it is ok to shift these tasks over there. To me it seems, that pool is intended for rather short-lived tasks that do not do heavy IO in comparison to the tasks that use the `SNAPSHOT` pool. And that is why we allow the `SNAPSHOT_META` pool to scale to a large number temporarily (since that wouldn't overwhelm the IO/Bandwidth on the node). By that logic, deletes and metadata work are also a good fit there. But I was curious if this is correct, and whether there are other reasons for the `SNAPSHOT_META` max size.

> that pool is intended for rather short-lived tasks that do not do heavy IO

Yes, this is it. Metadata writes and deletes are in-memory things in Elasticsearch, and they spend most of their time waiting for a response from the repository, so it makes sense to do them all in parallel where possible.

My thinking here is that uploading tiny metadata blobs is almost all waiting on the remote blob store, in contrast to uploading the data blobs which have similar overhead but then spend most of their time reading data off disk and sending it out over the wire.
Closing since this might cause more problems that it solves! See https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/93593#discussion_r1105710941

review_comment: Not sure what this value should be. I'm guessing we want it to be a fraction of the `SNAPSHOT_META` size.

This seems reasonable to me. My intuition is that deletes can sometimes take a while (when done in bulk) so we don't want to use up all the meta threads here. The meta pool is sized to `3*$PROCS` so this means we might have at most `$PROCS` delete tasks waiting.

AIUI we don't parallelise the deletes today much: each snapshot delete does all its blob deletes on a single thread, as does each snapshot finalization (which only deletes metadata).
Seems ok too, not sure this one really matters much.
:+1: definitely makes sense to me to parallelise harder the writing of updated metadata when deleting a snapshot
:+1: definitely makes sense to me to parallelise harder the writing of updated metadata when creating a snapshot

The risk here though, is that now a massive parallelisation (think first snapshot of 5k indices, writing 5k metadata files) will completely block the get-snapshots API or snapshot status APIs until it's through. I feel like that's an issue since we and Cloud won't be able to get a snapshot's status for an extended period of time potentially.
Ah ok that's a good point. Should we throttle here to keep the real queue size under control, or is this whole idea just not going to work?

I think if we want this, yes then we need to have some mechanism like the `ThrottledTaskRunner` in place to prevent from starvation on this pool.
I really do wonder if it's worth it messing with this though? In the end, if we really want finalisation faster we should introduce batching to it. It's really rare for finalisation to be slow on uploading index metadata ever since we deduplicate per-index for unchanged metadata, so this really only hits the first snapshot in a large cluster. 
Finalisation tends to just be slow since it's this multi-step process including CS updates and writing the heavy `RepositoryData` in the real world I think.

I thought something like this would have helped in the SDHE linked from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/93220 but I'm not convinced about that any more.

Still, this seems like a much smaller change than batched finalisations.

++ I'm not so sure this will be of much help with that issue. Intuitively I'd rather not break with the separate pools for read and write and have to mess with not blocking the pool in tricky ways unless we get a clear win from it.
ok, sorry @pxsalehi for the wild-goose chase here :)
